raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates near-complete opacification of the right hemithorax with a contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which is the classic radiological presentation of a massive pleural effusion causing compressive lung collapse. Pneumothorax would appear hyperlucent rather than opaque, and simple atelectasis typically causes an ipsilateral mediastinal shift.
